## TL;DR

The Settings and Agents pages were inventoried through the isolated auth-less development app, and a confirmed spend threshold validation defect was fixed with a component regression test. Follow-up verification now includes actual Settings and Agents edits that saved and survived a browser reload in a separate scratch root. This is stronger evidence than the original representative pass, but it is not evidence that every field and action was individually exercised. I recorded that boundary in the QA note rather than extrapolating from shared autosave behavior.

## Work and rationale

The first pass found that the spend alert threshold could silently reject a negative value and presented a fractional step despite the server accepting whole dollars. `SettingsView.vue` now reports a clear inline validation message, marks the field invalid for assistive technology, links the message through `aria-describedby`, rejects negative and fractional amounts without saving, and uses a whole-dollar step. The component test covers negative input, fractional input, error clearing, and saving a valid whole-dollar amount. This is the only confirmed defect from the QA pass, so I did not expand scope into speculative changes to unrelated settings.

Review round 3 correctly pointed out that the original note only demonstrated one save/reload example. I read the latest review report and returned to a separate scratch configuration rooted under this worktree. It has its own `repoos.toml` and is not the project's config. In Notifications I edited the threshold to 14 using keyboard input, waited for the UI's “Saved — applied live” status, reloaded the browser, and confirmed that 14 remained. The native stepper clamps a typed negative value to its minimum on blur in this browser; the component regression test is the evidence for the explicit validation message and the guarantee that invalid data is not saved. A browser accessibility value-set operation did not operate that stepper, so I switched to keyboard interaction and recorded that detail.

On the Agents page, I created a scratch-only custom agent role, observed the Saved state, reloaded, and confirmed the role remained. I then removed it and observed a second Saved state. Earlier work also edited the General tab's Areas field and confirmed it remained after reload. These checks exercised numeric, text, and collection save paths with real UI interactions. The Settings inventory includes General, Notifications, Security, Advanced, Import/Export, Support, and raw `repoos.toml`; the Agents inventory includes Agents, Build Your Team, Scheduled Tasks, Reminders, Detected Coding Agents, Model Playground, Model providers, Budget Controls, and Model routing.

The broader surface contains actions with effects beyond scratch configuration: sending provider requests or test notifications, granting browser notification permission, connecting integrations, installing background services, and changing automation or shared budget policy. I did not invoke those actions. Nor did I claim that every editable field had an individual valid/invalid/reload round trip. The settings form uses a shared changed-fields save path, but that common mechanism is not proof of each field's server validation, serialization, or reload behavior. The QA note names this remaining evidence boundary so a reviewer can distinguish observed behavior from inference.

## Approaches tried

I first used the task branch preview, which correctly presented the settings as read-only and therefore could not prove persistence. I then launched the built server in-process with auth disabled and a scratch root inside the worktree. Its visible project name and branch confirmed that Chrome was on the scratch app rather than another RepoOS instance. I used the actual browser UI, watched the save indicator, and reloaded the page. For the number input, direct accessibility value-setting did not produce an edit, so I entered the value through keyboard input. I used the component test to exercise validation edge cases that the browser's native number control normalizes on blur.

## Challenges and blockers

The Settings form includes many controls, while Agents includes both persisted configuration and operational actions. A literal per-control matrix needs separate valid, invalid (where applicable), save, and reload evidence for each editable field, plus careful exclusions for actions with external or host-level effects. The task's required local-only environment made it possible to test safe config changes but did not make provider, notification, permission, or OS-service actions safe to invoke. Browser host accessibility also differed from ordinary form inputs for the numeric stepper. As a result, the extended pass closes the representative-path gap and documents concrete exceptions, but does not claim exhaustive per-field coverage.

## Key learnings

An autosave banner and a shared save function are useful evidence, but neither proves that a particular field accepts, serializes, and reloads its value. Accessible numeric controls may also normalize invalid browser input before application-level feedback can be observed. Future QA passes should define a field inventory with evidence per field and distinguish pure configuration edits from operational actions before interacting with them. For this pass, the reliable evidence consists of a tested field-specific validation path, three UI save/reload examples across two page areas, and an explicit list of the unverified surface.
